manual: Instructions for the Experiment: Iodine Solution Reacting with Starch in Potato and AppleI. Basic Experiment InformationExperiment Title: Detection of Starch Using Iodine SolutionSubject: Natural Science – Cell & Developmental BiologyObjective: To identify the presence of starch in plant tissues by observing the color change caused by iodine solution, and to compare starch content in a potato and an apple through visual observation.II. Experimental MaterialsRaw potato slice, fresh apple slice, white plate, iodine solution, dropper, paper towel, camera or smartphone (fixed on a stand for time-lapse recording).III. Experimental Procedure1. Preparation: Place a raw potato slice and a fresh apple slice flat on a clean white plate, keeping them separate but within the same field of view.2. Camera Setup: Fix the camera focus and angle to clearly capture both slices; start recording or time-lapse mode.3. Iodine Application: Use a dropper to add 1–2 drops of iodine solution onto the surface of the potato slice, then add the same amount onto the apple slice.4. Observation: Allow the iodine to react for several seconds and continue recording to capture color changes.5. Completion: Stop recording after the color change stabilizes; clean up materials properly.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. Initial State: Both potato and apple slices are light-colored with no dark staining.2. After Adding Iodine: The potato slice surface gradually turns blue-black or dark purple where iodine is applied; the apple slice remains light yellow-brown with little or no color change.V. Summary of Experimental PrincipleIodine solution reacts specifically with starch to form a blue-black complex. Potatoes contain a high amount of starch stored in plant cells, so they show a strong color change. Apples contain much less starch (especially when fresh and ripe), so no obvious blue-black coloration appears. This color difference visually demonstrates the distribution of starch in different plant tissues.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Iodine is a chemical indicator for starch, producing a blue-black color when starch is present. Minimum assumptions: potato tissue contains abundant starch granules; apple tissue contains little starch; iodine is applied after placement of samples. Expected phenomena storyline: (1) static setup with potato and apple slices on a plate; (2) iodine droplets contact both surfaces; (3) within a short, accelerated time window, potato darkens visibly while apple remains largely unchanged. Verification requires a stable camera perspective, clear color contrast, and correct action-before-reaction sequencing.
